rows.speaker: الخليل ويونس
rows.claim: Al-Khalil and Yunus regard the repeated vocative patterns as equivalent and good Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: الخليل رحمه الله ويونس أن هذا كله سواء وهي لغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jarir’s يا تيم تيم عدى illustrates repeating a vocative name for emphasis; the first form remains as it would otherwise have been.
rows.anchor: يا تيم تيم عدى لا أبا لكم

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil compares the form to لا أبا لك: its first noun retains its expected form, while the lām phrase parallels the repeated second name.
rows.anchor: وقال الخليل رحمه الله هو مثل لا أبا لك

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil also parses يا تيم تيم عدى like يا تيم أخانا; the nominative construction is the regular analysis.
rows.anchor: وإن شئت قلت يا تيم تيم عدى كقولك يا تيم أخانا

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil treats يا طلحة like the repeated vocative: the combined name behaves as one, with final h sometimes present and sometimes omitted.
rows.anchor: الخليل رحمه الله أن قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first name’s tanwīn cannot be dropped outside the vocative; frequent use at the beginning of speech licenses this lightening.
rows.anchor: في غير النداء أن تذهب التنوين من الاسم الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjective forms follow the same vocative pattern: users of يا زيد الحسن say يا طلحة الحسن, and users of يا زيد الكريم say يا سلم الكريم.
rows.anchor: ومن قال يا زيد الحسن قال يا طلحة الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Light three-letter feminine land names, or names commonly treated as feminine, decline like قدر and شمس.
rows.anchor: على ثلاثة أحرف خفيفة وكان مؤنثا أو كان الغالب عليه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes are reported to take مصر in the verse as Egypt specifically.
rows.anchor: عن بعض المفسرين أن قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A foreign three-letter name is indeclinable even when light; examples include حمص and جور, as with longer feminine names.
rows.anchor: على ثلاثة أحرف أعجميا لم ينصرف وإن كان خفيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: واسط is usually masculine and declinable because it lies between Basra and Kufa; some Arabs instead make it feminine and indeclinable.
rows.anchor: وأما واسط فالتذكير والصرف أكثر وإنما سمي واسطا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masculine declension is best for دابق, though it can be feminine and indeclinable; Ghaylān’s verse illustrates masculine use.
rows.anchor: ودابق الصرف والتذكير فيه أجود قال الراجز وهو غيلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: منى is best treated as masculine and declinable, but feminine indeclinable use is also possible.
rows.anchor: أجود وإن شئت أنثت ولم تصرفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هجر is used as masculine or feminine; al-Farazdaq’s verse supplies feminine use, and Sibawayh also reports spoken usage.
rows.anchor: وكذلك هجر يؤنث ويذكر قال الفرزدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حجر اليمامة is masculine and declinable, though some treat حجر as feminine and indeclinable, like a woman named عمر.
rows.anchor: شيء مذكر سمي به المذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Land names vary in gender: عمان, الزاب, and إراب are feminine only, فلج masculine only, and adjectives can become place names.
rows.anchor: ومنها ما لا يكون إلا على التأنيث نحو عمان والزاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha al-Jaʿdī’s صفيح موضع shows an adjective used as a place name after removing the article, like واسط.
rows.anchor: ونابغة الجعدي بالرمل بيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs differ on قباء and حراء: some use masculine declension for place names, while others make them feminine and indeclinable as names of tracts.
rows.anchor: وأما قولهم قباء وحراء فقد اختلفت العرب فيهما فمنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أضاخ is feminine for some Arabs and masculine for others; al-Ajjāj’s verse attests masculine حراء.
rows.anchor: أنث وقال غيره فذكر وقال العجاج

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil says قباء should be declinable when used for a man: it is derivational and can be masculine, unlike established feminine names such as سعاد.
rows.anchor: وسألت الخليل فقلت أرأيت من قال هذه قباء

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil contrasts اللسان, established as feminine in that dialect and therefore indeclinable, with قباء and حواء, which are not fixed as feminine.
rows.anchor: وسألت الخليل فقلت أرأيت من قال هذه قباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Independent pronouns such as أنت and هو appear with predicates when Arabic cannot use the corresponding subject marker or clitic pronoun on a verb.
rows.anchor: كيف أنت وأين هو من قبل أنك لا تقدر على التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same constraint explains pronouns in clauses such as نحن وأنتم ذاهبون and جاء عبد الله وأنت.
rows.anchor: ومثل ذلك نحن وأنتم ذاهبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses هو after كأنه because the subject pronoun found in a finite verb cannot be expressed there as a clitic.
rows.anchor: @QB@ كأنه هو وأوتينا العلم @QE@

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The independent pronoun also appears after إلا in ما جاء إلا أنا; ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib supplies poetic evidence.
rows.anchor: قال عمرو بن معدى كرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forms such as ها أنا ذا and ها نحن أولاء use particles because a verbal subject marker or clitic pronoun is unavailable.
rows.anchor: وإنما استعملت هذه الحروف هنا لأنك لا تقدر

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil analyzes ها as the particle in هذا, with أنت inserted between ها and ذا; he similarly explains أنا هذا and هذا أنا.
rows.anchor: هي التي مع ذا إذا قلت هذا وإنما أرادوا

rows.speaker: أبو الخطاب
rows.claim: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb reports that trusted Arabs say أنا هذا and هذا أنا; a poem reflects shifting the conjunction between ها and ذا.
rows.anchor: أبو الخطاب أن العرب الموثوق بهم يقولون أنا هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ها أنت ذا, ها can instead be an attention particle, as shown by ها أنتم هؤلاء, where it follows أنتم rather than preceding the demonstrative.
rows.anchor: وقد تكون ها في ها أنت ذا غير مقدمة

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yunus reports هذا أنت as an attention-getting address meaning the person present is the one speaking, not an attempt to identify him as himself.
rows.anchor: حدثنا يونس أيضا تصديقا لقول أبي الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An initial ها is optional in this construction; ثم أنتم هؤلاء تقتلون أنفسكم shows the form without it.
rows.anchor: ثم أنتم هؤلاء تقتلون أنفسكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذن governs a following verb when it begins a reply, just as أرى governs a noun in its corresponding initial use.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن إذن إذا كانت جوابا وكانت مبتدأة عملت في الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An oath may separate إذن from its verb because إذن can be canceled or moved; أن and its sisters remain fixed at the beginning.
rows.anchor: ولا تفصل بين شيء مما ينصب الفعل وبين الفعل سوى إذن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sibawayh reports a muṣḥaf form and an Arab recitation with وإذن governing the subjunctive لا يلبثوا.
rows.anchor: وإذن لا يلبثوا خلفك إلا قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذن can be canceled after fa; the Qur’anic فإذن لا يؤتون الناس نقيرا exemplifies this non-governing use.
rows.anchor: وأما الإلغاء فقولك فإذن لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When إذن falls between a verb and its complement, or a clause depends on earlier speech, it is canceled and does not govern.
rows.anchor: إذا كانت بين الفعل وبين شيء الفعل معتمد عليه فإنها ملغاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAnama’s line is an exception because إذن begins a new, independent clause rather than depending on what precedes it.
rows.anchor: أردد حمارك لا تنزع سويته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An oath can make إذن non-governing when the clause depends on it; an initial إذن والله لا أفعل governs, unlike والله إذن أفعل.
rows.anchor: والله إذن لا أفعل من قبل أن أفعل معتمد على اليمين

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: With إن تأتني آتك وإذن أكرمك, a connected continuation takes the subjunctive; as a fresh future clause, indicative cancellation is also good according to Yunus.
rows.anchor: على قول من ألغى وهذا قول يونس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In إذن عبد الله يقول ذاك, إذن behaves like إنما or هل, not أن or كي, since those particles cannot precede a nominal clause.
rows.anchor: إذن عبد الله يقول ذاك لا يكون إلا هذا

rows.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
rows.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar reports Arabs answering with إذن أفعل ذاك; Yunus accepts the form as making إذن like هل or بل.
rows.anchor: عيسى بن عمر أن ناسا من العرب يقولون إذن أفعل ذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Present-state assumptions such as إذن أظنه فاعلا do not describe future actions; a future prediction would govern, as would a report of ongoing harm.
rows.anchor: أنك تلك الساعة في حال ظن وخيلة

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: A report that Al-Khalil posited an implicit أن after إذن would predict governing even when it is not warranted; Sibawayh says his own hearing supports the initial analysis.
rows.anchor: الخليل قال أن مضمرة بعد إذن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Frequent vague demonstratives develop exceptional forms like particles and interjections; when used as proper names, their special inflection follows those forms.
rows.anchor: فهذه الأسماء لما كانت مبهمة

rows.speaker: يونس والخليل
rows.claim: Yunus, Al-Khalil, and the grammarians Sibawayh met say ذا remains masculine as a name; ʿĪsā alone declines it for a woman named عمرو.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول يونس والخليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذي behaves like في, while تا behaves like لا.
rows.anchor: وأما ذي فبمنزلة في وتا بمنزلة لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ألاء can be fully declined as a man’s name; ألا is like هدى, and ألا and ألاء are variants like البكاء and البكاء.
rows.anchor: وأما ألاء فتصرفه اسم رجل وترفعه وتجره وتنصبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When الذي or التي becomes a man’s proper name, the article is removed because it names him rather than making him the relative pronoun’s referent.
rows.anchor: أخرجت الألف واللام لأنك تجعله علما له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With اللائي and اللاتي as names, the article is removed; retaining yā makes the form behave like قاضي, while deleting it allows full case inflection.
rows.anchor: وأما ألائي واللاتي فبمنزلة شائي وضاري وتخرج منه الألف واللام

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil leaves ذين unchanged as a man’s name because it remains a sound dual-shaped name.
rows.anchor: وسألت الخليل عن ذين اسم رجل فقال هو بمنزلة رجلين

words: نحن أولو قوة وأولو بأس شديد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sibawayh asks how أولو or ذوو behaves as a proper name; the answer gives ذوون and ألون outside an إضافة because the nūn drops only in construct forms.
rows.anchor: نحن أولو قوة وأولو بأس شديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A man named ذو مال remains unchanged, like ذو يزن: it is an إضافة form whose construct ending is retained, like أبو فلان.
rows.anchor: قالوا ذو يزن منصرف فلم يغيروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أمس is declinable as a man’s name; its fixed adverbial form and kasra arose from frequent use, like غاق, rather than case marking.
rows.anchor: عن أمس اسم رجل فقال مصروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذيت is like بنت and originally ذية; when its tā is removed, the form is treated heavily and tā is replaced by wāw as with أخت and بنت.
rows.anchor: أصلها ذية عمل بها ما عمل ببنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بنت and ابنة are originally فعل like أخت; أخوك and the reported plural آخاء support that analysis.
rows.anchor: أخوك وأخاك وأخيك وقول بعض العرب فيما زعم يونس آخاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nisba forms from ذية and ذيت are ذيوي because tā is retained; هنت and است likewise have a vowelled middle radical, as their plurals show.
rows.anchor: في الإضافة إلى ذية وذيت ذيوي فيهما وإنما منعك من ترك التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سه, ابن/بنون, and اثنتان/اثناء support a vowelled middle radical; هنت follows the common pattern, while ذيت is the exceptional non-declinable form.
rows.anchor: واثنتان بمنزلة ابنة أصلها فعل لأنه عمل بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلتا reflects a vowelled middle radical in كلا; an alternative treats its alif as feminine, and as a proper name it is diptote with tā like the wāw of شروى.
rows.anchor: وأما كلتا فيدلك على تحريك عينها قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In nisba, a deleted element is treated as absent from the base because the nisba yā follows the completed stem; thus ذيت is treated as though it had no tā and is lengthened.
rows.anchor: فكأنك ألحقت ياءي الإضافة اسما لم يكن فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فم derives from فوه, with mīm replacing wāw to create an ordinary-looking noun; the mīm behaves as the middle radical across cases.
rows.anchor: وأما فم فقد ذهب من أصله حرفان لأنه كان أصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq’s line هما نفثا في في من فمويهما attests restoration of the original form of فم in inflection.
rows.anchor: هما نفثا في في من فمويهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forms such as فموان restore the stem; addition restores it more strongly than dualization, while فمان allows either فموي or فمي.
rows.anchor: وقالوا فموان فإنما ترد في الإضافة كما ترد في التثنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A name ذو مال takes nisba as ذووي by restoring its base; similarly ذاه becomes ذووي, فو زيد is treated as فم, and شاء gives شاوي.
rows.anchor: وأما الإضافة إلى رجل اسمه ذو مال فإنك تقول ذووي
